title: Setting Up NextAuth.js
description: Add NextAuth.js to your app, configure a GitHub provider, and create your first session.

slides.title: Installation & First Config 📦
slides.content:
# Get NextAuth.js

```bash
npm install next-auth
```

We'll start with a GitHub provider (you need a GitHub OAuth App). But you can test locally with dummy credentials.

Create the API route file: `pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js`.

This catch‑all handles all auth actions (login, logout, callback).

slides.title: pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].js
slides.content: The minimal configuration with a GitHub provider.

quizData.question: Why does the NextAuth route file use `[...nextauth].js`?

options.text: To capture all sub‑paths like /api/auth/signin, /api/auth/callback, etc.
It's just a naming convention; any name works
To make it a dynamic route for user IDs

quizData.explanation: NextAuth uses a single catch‑all route to handle many endpoints like signin, signout, callbacks, and session retrieval.

slides.title: Environment Variables & OAuth 🔑
slides.content:
# Create a GitHub OAuth App

1. Go to GitHub Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps.
2. Create a new app.
3. Homepage URL: `http://localhost:3000`
4. Authorization callback URL: `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/github`

Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into `.env.local`:

```
GITHUB_ID=your_id
GITHUB_SECRET=your_secret
NEXTAUTH_SECRET=a_random_secret_string
NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
```

Generate a secret with `openssl rand -base64 32`.

slides.title: .env.local
slides.content: Never commit this file. Store secrets securely.

quizData.question: What must you set as the Authorization callback URL for a GitHub provider?
quizData.explanation: The callback URL follows the pattern `/api/auth/callback/{provider}`. GitHub redirects here after authentication.

slides.title: First Sign‑In ✨
slides.content:
# Start the dev server

Visit `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/signin`.

You'll see a default sign‑in page listing your configured providers. Click "Sign in with GitHub", authorize, and you're done!

Now your user session is stored in a secure HTTP‑only cookie.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content: For local development without a real OAuth app, use the **Credentials provider** or create a dummy GitHub app. Never skip the secret – it's used to encrypt the session cookie.
